title: India's New LPG Rules Mandate OTP Verification and Slash Subsidized Cylinders
excerpt: The central government's overhaul of cooking gas distribution requires Aadhaar-linked e-KYC, OTP-based delivery authentication, and cuts subsidized cylinders from nine to four per year under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana.
body:
• All domestic LPG deliveries now require OTP verification sent to the consumer's registered mobile number, along with a Delivery Authentication Code (DAC) system
  • Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana beneficiaries must complete Aadhaar-based e-KYC or risk losing their cooking gas subsidy entirely
  • Subsidized cylinders have been reduced from nine to four per year, while urban booking intervals have increased from 21 to 25 days
  • Households in areas with piped natural gas (PNG) availability may be required to surrender their LPG connections within three months

A Sweeping Overhaul of India's Cooking Gas System

India's cooking gas distribution network, which serves over 310 million active LPG connections, is undergoing its most significant regulatory shake-up in years. The central government has rolled out a series of measures designed to curb black marketing, eliminate duplicate connections, and ensure subsidies reach only verified beneficiaries.

The changes affect everything from how consumers book cylinders to how they receive them at their doorstep. For millions of low-income households that depend on subsidized cooking gas, the new rules carry real consequences — miss a verification deadline, and the subsidy stops.

OTP and DAC: Every Delivery Now Requires Authentication

Under the revised delivery protocol, receiving a domestic LPG cylinder now requires a valid one-time password (OTP) sent to the customer's registered mobile number. The delivery agent will not hand over the cylinder until the customer provides this code. Simply showing a booking receipt is no longer sufficient.

Alongside OTP verification, LPG distributors have introduced a Delivery Authentication Code (DAC) system. Once authentication succeeds, a digital cash memo — including the cylinder price, payment details, and delivery date — is sent directly to the consumer's phone. The system is already fully operational in Delhi, Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur, and Jaipur, and is expanding to all districts nationwide.

"The system generates this OTP automatically when the delivery agent arrives and scans the booking entry. Consumers must ensure their registered mobile number is active and updated with their gas distributor."

— Pune District Collector's Office, formal delivery order

e-KYC: The New Subsidy Gatekeeper

Beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) are now required to complete electronic Know Your Customer (e-KYC) verification — a biometric Aadhaar-linked process — to continue receiving subsidies. Those who failed to complete the process by the June 30 deadline may already have seen their subsidy payments suspended.

The verification can be completed through mobile apps from the three major oil marketing companies — IOC One, MyHPGas, or My Bharat Gas — or by visiting the nearest distributor with an Aadhaar card. Consumers whose Aadhaar-registered mobile number differs from their gas-registered number must update their details before the next booking cycle.

The government says the e-KYC drive is designed to identify individuals misusing multiple subsidized connections through different dealerships. The subsidy amount, currently ₹300 per cylinder, continues to be credited directly to the beneficiary's linked bank account — but only after successful verification.

Fewer Subsidized Cylinders and Longer Waits

The policy changes extend beyond verification. PMUY beneficiaries who previously received subsidies on nine cylinders annually will now receive subsidized pricing on just four cylinders per year. Any additional cylinders must be purchased at market rates.

Booking intervals have also been tightened. Urban consumers must now wait at least 25 days before booking a second 14.2 kg domestic cylinder, up from 21 days previously. In rural areas, the waiting period has increased to 45 days.

Officials say the booking interval change targets misuse rather than scarcity, emphasizing that India holds adequate LPG, petrol, and diesel stocks.

PNG Push: Surrender Your Cylinder or Lose It

In areas where piped natural gas is available, consumers face a new ultimatum. Under the revised rules, households with active PNG connections may be required to surrender their LPG cylinder within a prescribed time period — typically three months after notification. The government is actively pushing households to transition from cylinders to PNG, which it considers safer and more cost-effective for urban distribution.

What NRIs Should Watch For

For Indians living abroad who maintain LPG connections for family members back home, the e-KYC requirement adds a layer of urgency. Elderly parents or relatives who have not completed biometric verification risk losing subsidy access. The mobile-app-based verification is the simplest route, but those unfamiliar with the process may need in-person assistance at a distributor.

What's Next

The government has signaled that further digitization of the LPG distribution chain is planned, including expanded use of facial recognition and geo-tagged delivery tracking. With quarterly cylinder price revisions continuing and global crude oil markets remaining volatile, the squeeze on subsidized cooking gas is likely to tighten further in the months ahead.
nri_angle: NRIs maintaining LPG connections for family in India should ensure relatives complete mandatory e-KYC verification to avoid losing cooking gas subsidies.
